content.text:
I read the release and checked every figure, period and basis in the brief against it. Here is what I found.

**Facts.** Seven of the ten key facts are stated with correct figures, period and basis. The brief's weak spot is growth rates and special items: it reports dollar amounts for the revenue categories without the accompanying year-over-year growth (data processing +17%, international transaction +6%), omits the EPS growth rates, never mentions the $563 million severance special item, and never states the $6.2 billion combined share repurchase and dividend figure — it gives only the $4.9 billion repurchase component, which is a different number.

**Claims.** Every checkable assertion in the brief is supported by the release. I found no figure, period or basis error: $11.6B net revenue +14% (13% constant dollar), $5.6B/$2.97 GAAP, $6.3B/$3.32 non-GAAP, $4.8B GAAP opex +19% versus +17% non-GAAP opex, 71.7B processed transactions, and the capital return and balance sheet items all match. One nuance worth flagging even though I scored it supported: the brief's "$237 million litigation provision for the quarter" is the MDL special item the release excludes in its non-GAAP reconciliation; the GAAP litigation provision line for the quarter is $253 million. Analysts reading the brief could take the $237 million as the full GAAP charge.

facts.evidence: Net revenue was $11.6 billion, an increase of 14% (or 13% on a constant-dollar basis).
GAAP net income was $5.6 billion, or $2.97 per share. (Figure and basis correct; the brief does not give the 10% year-over-year growth.)
Non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion, or $3.32 per share. (Figure and basis correct; the brief does not give the 11% year-over-year growth.)
Revenue by category for the quarter: Data processing revenue was $6.0 billion... (Amount correct; the brief omits the 17% growth and does not identify it as the largest category.)

GAAP operating expenses were $4.8 billion, a 19% increase over the prior year." and "Track the trend of operating expenses, specifically personnel expenses, which were cited as a primary driver of the 19% increase in GAAP operating expenses.

Payments volume for the three months ended June 30, 2026, increased 10% over the prior year on a constant-dollar basis." and "cross-border volume excluding transactions within Europe increased 12% on a constant-dollar basis.
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
the company recorded a $237 million litigation provision for the quarter (MDL litigation provision correct; the $563 million severance special item is not mentioned anywhere in the brief).
international transaction revenue was $3.9 billion (amount correct; the brief omits the 6% growth and does not note it as the slowest category).

claims.claim: Visa reported 14% net revenue growth for the fiscal third quarter of 2026.
Net revenue was $11.6 billion, an increase of 14%.
Net revenue increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
GAAP net income was $5.6 billion.
GAAP earnings per share were $2.97.
Non-GAAP net income was $6.3 billion.
Non-GAAP earnings per share were $3.32.
GAAP operating expenses were $4.8 billion, a 19% increase over the prior year.
Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 17% over the prior year.
Total processed transactions for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were 71.7 billion, a 10% increase over the prior year.
Payments volume for the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased 10% over the prior year on a constant-dollar basis.
Total cross-border volume on a constant-dollar basis increased 13% over the prior year.
Cross-border volume excluding transactions within Europe increased 12% on a constant-dollar basis.
Data processing revenue for the quarter was $6.0 billion.
Service revenue for the quarter was $4.9 billion.
International transaction revenue for the quarter was $3.9 billion.
Other revenue for the quarter was $1.5 billion.
The release provides no guidance or outlook.
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
During the three months ended June 30, 2026, Visa repurchased approximately 14.5 million shares of class A common stock for $4.9 billion.
The board of directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.670 per share of class A common stock on July 28, 2026.
Remaining authorized funds for share repurchases were $28.4 billion as of June 30, 2026.
The company recorded a $237 million litigation provision for the quarter.
claims.note: Release identifies $237 million as the MDL litigation provision special item excluded in the non-GAAP reconciliation; the GAAP litigation provision line for the quarter is $253 million, so the brief's phrasing is imprecise but the figure is stated in the release.

claims.claim: Visa deposited $250 million into its litigation escrow account on June 25, 2026.
Personnel expenses were cited as a primary driver of the 19% increase in GAAP operating expenses.
The exchange offer for class B-1 and class B-2 common stock settled on May 12, 2026.
